messages:
jess: Heads up — after the latest model canary in us-west we started seeing 95th tail jumps from ~30ms to ~120ms on dedicated pools. GPU % looks fine, but latency correlates with a spike in outbound queue depth on a subset of hosts.

alvin: link to dashboards? which pool and time window?

jess: us-west-dedicated-3, window 11:12–11:24 UTC. dashboard: /dash/latency?range=12m (paste below). traces show many small prefill requests stacked.

marta: pulled NIC counters from the hosts — tx_queue_length and tx_dropped both spike. looks like big fanout around the same time. suspect KV prefetch fanout (siblings warming kvcache simultaneously).

ben: that matches tenant X behaviour — they pushed a rollout that aggressively prefetches prefixes. Could be bursting their egress and hitting NIC queue limits which then adds ~100ms of enqueueing.

jess: snippet from request logs around 11:15:
```
[11:15:03] prefill start tenant=X keys=64 concurrency=32
[11:15:03] outgoing packets queued 450 -> tx_drop=3
[11:15:03] reply latency 98ms
```

alvin: do we have per-tenant egress shaping enabled? we should have soft limits but maybe prefill bypasses them.

marta: prefill uses short-lived connections and can create bursts. NIC scheduler (pf_ring/driver) doesn't like that pattern. short-term mitigation: cap prefill concurrency and add jitter on our scheduler.

ben: operational quick-fix: reduce tenant X prefetch concurrency from 32 -> 6 and set prefill_jitter=150ms. I can put this as a kinetic override for the next 2h and watch. cost impact minimal.

jess: +1 to quick-fix, want to keep canary running though — reduce to 10% rollout and apply tenant override to the offending tenant only.

alvin: creating a throttling override now: `curl -XPOST https://ops-api/overrides -d '{"tenant":"X","prefill_concurrency":6,"ttl":"2h"}'`

sre-bot: alert history for us-west-dedicated-3: 2023-11-13T11:14:50Z spike detected (95p latency) — auto-sampled traces attached.

deploy-bot: Throttling override applied to tenant X (request id: e3a9).

marta: follow-up patch idea: scheduler-side scatter/gap for prefill: when a new allocation warms kvcache, scatter its fanout over 500–2000ms with per-host jitter so siblings don't align. I'll draft a change.

ben: also consider a per-pool outbound-queue-aware backoff: if tx_queue > threshold, reduce tenant prefill rate dynamically. That would give graceful self-throttle without human overrides.

jess: monitoring graphs are already looking better 2m after the override. 95p back ~35ms. Good signal.

alvin: next steps: 1) keep override for 2h, 2) marta to send scheduler PR with scatter + jitter, 3) ben to prototype queue-aware feedback loop, 4) follow up postmortem with tenant X to tune their rollout.

marta: will open PR and include benchmark where we simulate 50 concurrent warmers.

ben: rough cost estimate for mitigation features: dev + 2 days infra work, negligible infra run cost.

jess: thanks everyone. leaving canary at 10% and watching for 20m. ping if any regressions. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: note: add incident tag `noisy-prefill-fanout` if we need a full incident.
